proof_summary: Take \(n=716{,}993{,}899\), so the relevant odd integer is \(1{,}433{,}987{,}797\); the exponents are bounded by \(1\le x,y\le30\). A finite check uses residues modulo \(6\) to eliminate every pair except even–even pairs, excludes oversized sums, and exhibits a proper divisor of the residual \(1{,}433{,}987{,}797-2^x-7\cdot2^y\) in every remaining case, proving that this new index also has value zero.
